A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and retain matching optimization benchmarks. All 26 pages of v3 and 24 pages of v4, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original repeated optimization experiments, surrogate-prediction results, ablations and computational timings in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original optimization results, initialization experiments and gradient diagnostics in Sections 4–6 and Appendix C, including synthetic experiments repeated twenty times.

M1.justification: v4 Section 5 introduces dimension-dependent length-scale initialization, ℓ0 = c√d, with c = 1 in experiments, producing SBO-SE(RI). This adds an explicit procedure for preventing SE-kernel training failure that v3 did not propose. Existing Matérn MAP/MLE and single-length-scale variants largely remain under revised names or appendix placement.

E1.justification: The eleven main BO benchmarks remain, but v3's separate ten-dataset surrogate-prediction evaluation is removed rather than relocated. v4 retains narrower prediction checks on Hartmann6/Rosenbrock and Mopta08/DNA, substantially reducing prediction-task coverage. The briefly reported polynomial-optimization experiment in v3 Appendix B.1 also disappears.

E2.justification: VBO is newly evaluated in the main BO comparisons, and log-EI joins the acquisition-function comparison. Removing the regression study also removes its ProjGP, AddGP and SaasBO surrogate comparisons. BNN Laplace/HMC remain in v4 Appendix C.1, so their absence from the main figures is not an overall removal.

E3.justification: v3 Appendix B.3's kernel-learning experiment becomes a crossed dimension/initialization study in v4 Section 4, extending the dimension range from 50–300 to 50–600 and measuring gradients and parameter changes alongside MSE instead of reporting test log likelihood. The SE BO comparison is now specified with L-BFGS MAP training in v4 Section 6.1, whereas v3 Appendix B.3 specified MLE.

E4.justification: v4 adds initialization sensitivity experiments and direct gradient/update measurements during training and SVM/Rosenbrock BO runs, linking failure to the proposed remedy in Figures 1–2. It also tests log-EI rather than merely suggesting it. v3's quantitative prior-sensitivity prediction Tables 8–9 disappear; MAP/MLE/NUTS and UCB exploration analyses largely remain.

E5.justification: The redesigned Hartmann6/Rosenbrock experiment reports twenty repetitions per dimension and initialization, versus five repetitions for v3 Appendix B.3's experiment. This does not establish additional runs of unchanged experiments. BO comparisons retain ten-run reporting and variability displays.

E6.justification: v4 adds initialization-dependent failure thresholds, RI/VBO optimization results and log-EI scores, while removing v3's regression Tables 4, 5, 8 and 9. The main SVM Matérn outcome changes from approximately -0.14 in v3 Figure 2 to -0.05 in v4 Figure 4, but v4 Figure 7 retains the older MAP range; this is not a verified same-setting gain. Timing values in v3 Tables 6–7 are unchanged in v4 Tables 4–5.

T1.justification: v3 provides standard GP/BO formulas and a heuristic explanation of SE-kernel decay. v4 adds gradient derivations, threshold Propositions 4.1 and 4.3, probability-bound Lemma 4.2 and initialization Lemma 5.1. New Appendix A supplies proofs, with the probability bounds assuming independently sampled uniform inputs.

C1.justification: v4 makes identifying a training-failure mechanism and proposing theoretically motivated initialization central contributions. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion newly claim that suitable initialization can restore strong SE-kernel BO performance. The Matérn performance headline remains, while the separate ten-dataset surrogate-learning contribution is dropped.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix B.3 emphasizes rapid covariance decay and potentially inadequate SE modeling capacity. v4 instead attributes failure primarily to initialization-induced vanishing gradients and explains why Matérn kernels and larger initial length-scales help. It also connects concentrated priors to this mechanism. New Appendix D explicitly acknowledges that the maximum workable input dimensionality remains unknown.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly discloses the default initialization of approximately 0.693, additional NUTS prior choices and the BoTorch log-EI implementation. It removes v3's experiment-code link and explicit 400/300-step budget sentence, although those budgets remain visible in plots. Hardware information and most baseline implementation sources are retained.

R1.justification: The structural-BO related-work discussion largely remains. v4 adds Bengio/Hanin gradient-vanishing citations, removes the Batlle operator-learning connection and Li BNN-study discussion, and expands the already-cited Hvarfner/VBO work into a focused comparison between dimension-dependent prior regularization and initialization.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, result discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten around initialization and gradient failure. GP background is compressed, related-work subsections are flattened, and training/BNN analyses are reorganized into the appendices. New proof and limitations sections change the narrative structure; the author list also expands.

P2.justification: v4 adds gradient-diagnostic plots and threshold tables, redraws main comparison panels for RI/VBO, and consolidates trajectory displays using best/median/worst baseline summaries. BNN/training displays and timing tables move, while regression tables and several standalone endpoint plots disappear. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially advances v3's tentative explanation of SE failure by connecting initialization to gradient diagnostics, formal bounds and an experimentally tested remedy in Sections 4–5 and Figures 1–5. This improves both explanatory and practical value. The bounds remain limited by their sampling assumptions, and removing regression comparisons and the code link reduces breadth and reproducibility. The unexplained main/appendix SVM discrepancy limits confidence in exact scores, but the broader mechanism-and-remedy evidence supports a substantial net improvement.
